chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Musa ibn Bakr who said:

I said to Zurarah: Indeed, Bukayr narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that the shares of brothers (from the father) and sisters (from father and mother) are increased and decreased, because their shares are not greater than the share of brothers and sisters (from father and mother) if they were in their place.
Because Allah, the Mighty and Glorious, says: 'If a man dies leaving no child, and he has a sister, then she receives one-half of what he left; and he inherits her if she leaves no child.'

He says that he inherits all her property if she leaves no child. Despite this, they give the complete share to the one whom Allah has specified as receiving one-half, and they give to the one whom Allah has specified as receiving the entire property less than one-half. And the woman's share is never more than the man's share if he were in her place.
He said: Then Zurarah said, 'This is established among our companions; they do not differ regarding it.'

key_terms.الأخَوَاتِ لِلأبِ وَالأمِّ: Sisters from father and mother (full sisters)
key_terms.الإخْوَةُ لِلأبِ: Brothers from the father (half-siblings sharing the father)
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurarah ibn A'yan, a prominent Shia scholar
key_terms.يَرِثُهَا: He inherits her (the male sibling inherits the female's share in absence of children)

ai.seo_question: How are the inheritance shares of half-siblings adjusted according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'al-zawaj' (adjustment) in inheritance, where the shares of half-siblings are calibrated to ensure they never exceed the portion full siblings would receive in their stead. Citing Surah An-Nisa 4:176, the narrator Musa ibn Bakr demonstrates this logic through the sister's fixed half-share, while Zurarah affirms that this specific ruling is a consensus (ijma') among the Shia scholars, distinguishing it from other schools of thought.

en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Flassan ibn Ali from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Musa ibn Bakr who has narrated the following: “

I once said to Zurarah that ibn Bukayr has narrated to me from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that the shares of brothers from the father and sisters from father and mother increase and decrease. It is because their shares are not greater than the share of brothers and sisters from father and mother if they were in their place.

Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, ‘. . . if a man dies who does not leave behind a child and he has a sister, she receives one-half of the legacy and he receives the entire legacy if she does not leave behind any children.’

He says that he receives the entire legacy, which she leaves behind if she does not leave behind a child. Despite this, they give complete to one whose share Allah has mentioned as One-half and they give less than One-half to one whom Allah has given the entire legacy. The share of woman is never more than the share of man if he was in her place.
He (the narrator) has said that Zurarah then said, ‘This is applied by our people without any difference.’”
